answer: Stratified random re-audit resists sybil graders: the re-audit sample is STRATIFIED to over-sample grades from suspicious strata — new graders, outlier scorers, tight clusters — so collusion-prone grading faces a higher check probability than the baseline. A crystal-clear honest veteran is rarely re-audited; a walnut-dense ring in a flagged stratum is checked often, and a FAIL against the objective ground truth slashes the cluster. The orchard of grades is sampled where risk concentrates, so colluders cannot hide in the low-scrutiny bulk.
